title: Exceptional scalar mate equation from normalized integration
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to A'$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings, and let $f:X\to Y$ be a compactifiable separated finite-type map between Noetherian schemes. Work in the ordinary small-etale derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with scalar tensor $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^LA'$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Write $F_R=Rf_{!,R}$ and let $R_R$ be its actual right adjoint with counit $\varepsilon_R$, for $R=A,A'$ [def-amb-etale-compact-support, thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Use the canonical proper/open scalar map $q_M:Q_YF_AM\xrightarrow{\sim}F_{A'}Q_XM$ of [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence], including its projection square, and the normalized tensor and unit identifications. Set
$$b_K:Q_XR_AK\to R_{A'}Q_YK$$
to be the adjoint transpose of $Q_Y(\varepsilon_{A,K})q_{R_AK}^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. In particular $q_{R_AK}$ is invertible even at $K=A_Y[0]$.

Let $W\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, $W'\in D(X_{\mathrm{et}},A')$, $l:Q_XW\xrightarrow{\sim}W'$ and traces $t_A:F_AW\to A_Y$, $t_{A'}:F_{A'}W'\to A'_Y$ satisfy
$$t_{A'}F_{A'}(l)q_W=u_YQ_Y(t_A),$$
where $u_Y:Q_YA_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}A'_Y$ is coefficient-unit multiplication. Assume the projection maps with $W,W'$ are invertible on all inputs. Put $G_{0,A}K=f_A^*K\otimes_A^LW$ and $c_{A,K}=(1_K\otimes t_A)P_{f,A;K,W}^{-1}$, and define the primed objects and maps similarly. Let $\gamma_{A,K}:G_{0,A}K\to R_AK$ and $\gamma_{A',L}:G_{0,A'}L\to R_{A'}L$ be their actual adjoint transposes. Let $a_K:Q_XG_{0,A}K\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{0,A'}Q_YK$ be the scalar tensor/pullback comparison followed by $l$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Then
$$Q_Y(c_{A,K})q_{G_{0,A}K}^{-1}=c_{A',Q_YK}F_{A'}(a_K),$$
and
$$b_KQ_X(\gamma_{A,K})=\gamma_{A',Q_YK}a_K.$$
If the gamma components in this equation are invertible, then $b_K$ is invertible. These equations include $K=A_Y[0]$ with the normalized scalar/single coefficient-unit comparison; there is no assumption that taking a mate preserves arbitrary isomorphisms, nor any flatness assumption on $A'$ over $A$.

proof.text:
Fix $K$ and abbreviate $F=F_A$, $F'=F_{A'}$, $G=G_{0,A}K$, $P=P_{f,A;K,W}$ and $P'=P_{f,A';Q_YK,W'}$. Let $s:Q_Y(K\otimes_A^LFW)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_YK\otimes_{A'}^LQ_YFW$ be the normalized tensor comparison, and let $h:Q_XG\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{A'}^*Q_YK\otimes_{A'}^LQ_XW$ be the scalar tensor/pullback comparison. Thus $a_K=(1\otimes l)h$. The all-input projection square of [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence], using the canonical comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback], reads with every comparison displayed
$$F'(h)q_GQ_Y(P)=P_{f,A';Q_YK,Q_XW}(1\otimes q_W)s.$$
Its source is $Q_Y(K\otimes_A^LFW)$, and its target is $F'(f_{A'}^*Q_YK\otimes_{A'}^LQ_XW)$. No boundedness hypothesis is needed for this clause.

source.place: paragraph 2: coefficient compatibility of integration; expand the ordered scalar/projection square

proof.text:
The projection transformation in [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence] is natural in its second input. Apply that naturality to $l:Q_XW\to W'$:
$$F'(1\otimes l)P_{f,A';Q_YK,Q_XW}=P'(1\otimes F'(l)).$$
Postcomposing Step 1 with $F'(1\otimes l)$ therefore gives
$$F'(a_K)q_GQ_Y(P)=P'(1\otimes F'(l)q_W)s.$$
This is substitution into a naturality square, with the specified $a_K$, rather than a new comparison theorem.

source.place: paragraph 2: coefficient compatibility; naturality in the orientation coefficient

proof.text:
Postcompose the equation of Step 2 with $c_{A',Q_YK}=(1\otimes t_{A'})P'^{-1}$. By the assumed trace equation and functoriality of tensor, its right side becomes
$$(1\otimes t_{A'}F'(l)q_W)s=(1\otimes u_YQ_Y(t_A))s=Q_Y(1_K\otimes t_A).$$
The last equality uses the stated normalized unit identifications: naturality of the tensor comparison first gives $s_{K,A_Y}Q_Y(1_K\otimes t_A)=(1\otimes Q_Y(t_A))s$, and $(1\otimes u_Y)s_{K,A_Y}$ is the scalar extension of the unitor. These are precisely the ordinary-balancing tensor and unit normalizations of [def-pur-exceptional-coefficient-normalizations]. Thus
$$c_{A',Q_YK}F'(a_K)q_GQ_Y(P)=Q_Y(1_K\otimes t_A).$$
Since $P$ is invertible by hypothesis and $q_G$ is invertible by [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence], compose on the right with $Q_Y(P^{-1})q_G^{-1}$. This proves
$$c_{A',Q_YK}F'(a_K)=Q_Y(c_{A,K})q_G^{-1}.$$ In Lean the existing theorem tensorIso_right_unit of [lem-pur-scalar-right-unit] supplies precisely the displayed right-unitor normalization.

source.place: paragraph 2: coefficient-compatible traces imply the scalar integration equation

proof.text:
Write $\varepsilon'=\varepsilon_{A',Q_YK}$ and $\gamma=\gamma_{A,K}$. The definition [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of the specified mate gives
$$\varepsilon'F'(b_K)=Q_Y(\varepsilon_{A,K})q_{R_AK}^{-1}.$$
Naturality of the isomorphism $q$ in [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence], applied to $\gamma:G\to R_AK$, gives
$$q_{R_AK}^{-1}F'(Q_X\gamma)=Q_Y(F\gamma)q_G^{-1}.$$
Substitute these two equations and use the defining transpose equation $\varepsilon_{A,K}F(\gamma)=c_{A,K}$. The inverse adjoint transpose of $b_KQ_X\gamma$ is consequently
$$\varepsilon'F'(b_KQ_X\gamma)=Q_Y(\varepsilon_{A,K})Q_Y(F\gamma)q_G^{-1}=Q_Y(c_{A,K})q_G^{-1}.$$

source.place: paragraph 2, final sentence: transpose the coefficient equality using the actual counit mate

proof.text:
Put $\gamma'=\gamma_{A',Q_YK}$. By its defining transpose equation, the inverse adjoint transpose of $\gamma'a_K$ is
$$\varepsilon'F'(\gamma'a_K)=c_{A',Q_YK}F'(a_K).$$
Step 3 identifies this with the final expression of Step 4. The adjunction Hom bijection is injective, so the original arrows agree:
$$b_KQ_X(\gamma_{A,K})=\gamma_{A',Q_YK}a_K.$$
Here inverse transposition is $v\mapsto\varepsilon'F'(v)$, the same adjunction convention used in [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. This uses equality of specified transposes, not any assertion that mates preserve isomorphisms.

source.place: paragraph 2, final sentence: transposing the trace equalities proves compatibility

proof.text:
If the two gamma components are invertible, functoriality gives $(Q_X\gamma_{A,K})^{-1}=Q_X(\gamma_{A,K}^{-1})$. Step 5 then expresses
$$b_K=\gamma_{A',Q_YK}a_K\,Q_X(\gamma_{A,K}^{-1}),$$
a composite of isomorphisms, since $a_K$ is an isomorphism by its construction. All preceding equations were for arbitrary $K$ on the unbounded categories. In particular $K=A_Y[0]$ is permitted: [lem-pur-etale-compact-scalar-coherence] makes $q_{R_A(A_Y[0])}$ invertible without requiring any bound on that right-adjoint object. The multiplication unit and tensor comparisons of [def-pur-exceptional-coefficient-normalizations] identify $Q_Y(A_Y[0])$ with $A'_Y[0]$ and the unit-input tensor factors with $W,W'$. Substituting this input into Steps 1--5 gives exactly the single coefficient-unit equation stipulated in the statement. No step imposed flatness on $A'$ over $A$.
